steps.label: Does equal-area HEALPix gridding remove latitude bias from the power spectrum of satellite imagery?
steps.text: For Earth-observation satellite imagery, does computing the angular power spectrum on an equal-area HEALPix grid, compared with a regular geographic lon/lat grid, remove the latitude-dependent area bias in the spectral amplitude?

components.label: Population
components.text: Earth-observation optical satellite imagery (multispectral surface-reflectance scenes) at regional scale.

components.label: Intervention
components.text: Angular power spectrum analysis performed on an equal-area HEALPix tessellation of the sphere defined on the WGS84 ellipsoid.

components.label: Comparator
components.text: The same analysis on a regular geographic latitude/longitude grid, whose cells shrink in surface area towards the poles.

components.label: Outcome
components.text: Presence or absence of a latitude-dependent bias in the spectral amplitude / power as a function of spatial scale.

steps.text: Computing the angular power spectrum of satellite imagery on an equal-area HEALPix grid removes the latitude-dependent area bias that a regular longitude/latitude grid introduces.

steps.label: Equal-area HEALPix removes latitude bias from the power spectrum of satellite imagery

steps.scope:
Whether the equal-area property of a HEALPix grid yields an angular power spectrum of an optical satellite scene that is free of the latitude-dependent
area weighting a lon/lat grid imposes. In scope: a single regional Sentinel-2 L2A reflectance window analysed end to end on equal-area HEALPix. 

Out of scope: a fully quantified side-by-side lon/lat baseline, multi-scene statistics, atmospheric/cloud effects, and other sensors.
steps.method:
Read a window of Sentinel-2 L2A band B04 directly from the public AWS Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF archive. Compute the window's lon/lat bounding box and
tile it with HEALPix cells on the WGS84 ellipsoid at depth 18 using GRID4EARTH healpix-geo (make_healpix_rectangle_from_lonlat / zone_coverage). Sample the
reflectance at each equal-area cell centre, resample to a regular grid, apodise with a Tukey window, and compute the radially-averaged isotropic power spectrum
with GRID4EARTH healpix-analyse (ps). Because every HEALPix cell covers the same surface area, the spectrum carries no latitude-dependent area weighting. The
whole pipeline is orchestrated by a Snakemake workflow and runs from the public COG in seconds.
steps.deviations: Question-rooted: there is no prior equal-area-HEALPix power-spectrum pipeline for Sentinel-2 to deviate from. This is a fresh application of the equal-area approach using the GRID4EARTH stack.

steps.label: Sentinel-2 equal-area HEALPix power-spectrum outcome
steps.conclusion:
The angular power spectrum of a Sentinel-2 scene can be computed end to end on an equal-area HEALPix grid on the WGS84 ellipsoid with the GRID4EARTH stack
(healpix-geo + healpix-analyse). Because every HEALPix cell covers the same surface area, the resulting spectrum carries none of the latitude-dependent area
weighting that a lon/lat grid would impose — supporting the claim by construction. The spectrum shows the expected monotonic power-law fall-off with
spatial frequency, the signature of a natural surface-reflectance field.
steps.evidence:
Configuration and result recorded in results/powerspectrum.json:
- scene S2A_22WEV_20190723, band B04 (red, 10 m), 256×256 px window (~2.6 km)
- equal-area HEALPix at depth 18 (nside = 262144), ellipsoid = WGS84
- field sampled at equal-area cell centres, then radially-averaged isotropic power spectrum computed with healpix-analyse `ps`
- the spectrum (results/powerspectrum.png) falls off monotonically with spatial frequency on a log–log axis (power-law behaviour), with no latitude-dependent amplitude term, because the cells are equal-area by construction.

Github repository: https://github.com/annefou/healpix-analyse-s2-powerspectrum
steps.limitations:
The repo demonstrates the equal-area pipeline rather than quantifying the lon/lat bias it avoids: no side-by-side lon/lat baseline spectrum is computed here, so
the bias magnitude is argued by construction, not measured. Single scene, single band, single date; no atmospheric, cloud, or coastal effects; generalisation to other sensors and to a controlled multi-latitude comparison is left to follow-up.
